entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.
Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

3. None appears on behalf of the respondent no.2 despite service of notice.2.
4.
This is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant.
The first bail application was rejected by this Court for want of prosecution on 31.10.2022.
5. Learned counsel while arguing the second bail application, learned counsel for the applicant argued that the F.I.R. in question was lodged as a missing person report.

Subsequently, in the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim admitted that she knew the applicant for the last two years and had gone out of her own free will and when they were going on a train, they were apprehended.
There was slight variance in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

However,
Pintu Kushwaha vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6650967/
1 she admitted that she stayed with the applicant for a term of five days.

entities.text: Pintu Kushwaha vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The tentative age of the victim is 17 years.
The victim did not support the prosecution story and the victim even refused to undergo medical examination.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that prima facie, there is no definite document to conclusively form an opinion with regard to the age of the victim at this stage and the same shall be decided by the trial court.
The applicant is in custody since 2.10.2021 having no criminal antecedents hence the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
7. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail.

8. Considering the statements of the victim under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. whereby the victim has not supported the prosecution story and the victim has refused to undergo medical examination coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 2.10.2021 having no criminal antecedents, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
9. Accordingly, the second bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant Pintu Kushwaha be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.220 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 343 I.P.C., Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Behtagujawar, District Unnao on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
